record.paper_title: Selected results and open problems in a semiclassical theory of dense matter
record.context_brief: Linking SK theory to statistical physics
record.original_question: Although the SK semiclassical theory has produced useful numerical results, its formulation is described as unusual and this is presented as an obstacle to broader uptake. Can the SK theory be placed within the established framework of statistical physics by giving a systematic correspondence between its parameters and standard statistical-physics variables, so that the theory is no longer an isolated formalism but a special or derived case within a recognized framework?

evidence.quote: An even more interesting problem would be to link the SK theory to the well established theoretical framework of statistical physics.Although the SK theory has given good results in a range of applications,its unusal formulation hinders its wider spread in the research community.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The Savić–Kašanin (SK) semiclassical theory of dense matter is a phenomenological framework introduced for describing properties of matter at high pressures and densities (phase transitions, metallization pressures, equations of state of planetary interiors, etc.). It postulates relations between macroscopic quantities — such as molar volume, pressure, temperature, and a small set of material-dependent constants — through a system of semi-empirical equations whose structure does not obviously arise from a standard statistical-mechanical partition function or free-energy functional.

Problem. Provide a systematic embedding of the Savić–Kašanin theory into the standard framework of equilibrium statistical physics. Concretely, exhibit a microscopic or coarse-grained model (specified by a Hamiltonian, a free-energy functional, or a well-defined statistical ensemble) together with an explicit correspondence
\[
\Phi : \{\text{SK parameters and state variables}\} \longrightarrow \{\text{standard statistical-physics variables (temperature, chemical potential, density, partition function, thermodynamic potentials, correlation functions, …)}\},
\]
such that the constitutive equations and predictions of the SK theory are recovered, in a specified regime, as a special case, limit, or controlled approximation of the chosen statistical-physics model. The correspondence should identify each SK constant with a well-defined statistical-mechanical quantity and clarify the approximations (e.g., mean-field, semiclassical, low-temperature, high-density) under which the SK relations follow.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned background information about Kirzhnits-type semiclassical expansions and applications of the Savić–Kašanin semiclassical theory to dense matter (phase transitions, metallization pressures), but no source was found that establishes a systematic embedding of the SK theory into the standard framework of statistical physics with an explicit dictionary between SK parameters and statistical-mechanical variables. The status of this question therefore appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Selected results and open problems in a semiclassical theory of dense matter
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses applications of the SK semiclassical theory of dense matter and lists linking it to statistical physics as an open direction.
status_evidence.claim: The connection of the SK theory to standard statistical physics is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Selected results and open problems in a semiclassical theory of dense matter (PDF)
status_evidence.snippet: Describes the SK semiclassical theory of Savić and Kašanin applied to dense matter and notes its unusual formulation as a barrier to wider use.
status_evidence.claim: No subsequent systematic statistical-physics embedding of the SK theory is identified in the accessible literature.
